title: Spec-Driven Development: Agentic Coding at FAANG Scale and Quality — Al Harris, Amazon Kiro
talk_summary: Al Harris (Amazon Kiro) presents spec-driven development: turning a prompt into structured EARS requirements, a design doc, correctness properties, and a task list, then executing tasks one at a time. The transferable mechanisms are structured artifacts as the control surface, explicit test cases baked into task definitions, steering docs as persistent memory, and keeping agent context small with tool-driven self-discovery.

takeaways.technique: Spec artifacts as the unit of work (requirements → design → task list)
takeaways.what_they_do: Each feature becomes a spec folder with structured requirements (EARS 'when/then/shall' syntax), a design doc, and a task list; tasks are executed one at a time against the spec, and later changes mutate the existing spec rather than accreting new ones.

takeaways.technique: Explicit test cases embedded in task definitions
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of task bullets that just restate acceptance criteria, they ask the agent to enumerate the concrete unit test cases that must pass before the task is 'done', then use hooks to enforce them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the LMS are very good at saying I'm done. I'm happy... The tests don't pass but they're annoying. I tried three times them to work. I'm just going to move on

takeaways.technique: Steering docs written from painful learnings
takeaways.what_they_do: When the human figures out a non-obvious operational detail (a required CLI flag, deploy sequence), they tell the agent to write it into a steering doc, which is then loaded as persistent project memory.
takeaways.evidence_quote: once I go through that pain of learning I just say kira write what you learned into a steering doc and it will usually do a very good job of summarizing

takeaways.technique: Small context + tool-driven self-discovery over big indexes
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately keep the agent's context small and give it search/fetch tools to find what it needs, rather than stuffing codebase or docs into the prompt; indexing is used for UI search, not fed to the agent.

takeaways.technique: Optimize for prompt-cache hit rate over summarization
takeaways.what_they_do: They avoid mid-session pruning/summarization because it breaks prompt caching; they keep the prefix stable to get high cache-token usage per turn, and only summarize at the hard cap.
takeaways.numbers: 90-95% cached token usage per turn; ~200k token cap; summarization takes 30-45s

takeaways.technique: Use MCP servers during spec/design phases, not just coding
takeaways.what_they_do: They wire MCP servers (task tracker, docs, fetch/search) into the requirements and design phases so the agent pulls real external data and can challenge the human's implicit assumptions with researched alternatives.
